newsitem.title: USA: Digital seen reporting higher Q4 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Digital seen reporting higher Q4 earnings.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp is expected to report higher fiscal fourth quarter earnings on Thursday, but revenues and sales of its Alpha-based systems are expected to be down from last year, analysts said.

Analysts surveyed by First Call expect DEC to report earnings of $0.73 per share. A year earlier, the company posted a profit of $0.33 a share before a restructuring charge of $492 million to pay for job cuts and plant closings.
"It will be respectable," Jay Stevens, an analyst with Buckingham Research Group Inc, said of DEC's fourth quarter results. "People might latch onto that to say there's improvement at DEC."
Stevens said he recently raised his earnings estimate for DEC by $0.05 to match the Wall Street consensus.
He said he would not be surprised if the company reported even higher earnings.
DEC Chief Executive Robert Palmer said at the end of the third quarter in April that he was disappointed with a year-over-year decline in revenues.
He said it might take a few quarters to turn the situation around.
Steve Smith, an analyst with Paine Webber, said of the fourth quarter results, "We're looking for a four percent revenue decline."
DEC had revenues of $3.72 billion in the fourth quarter last year.
DEC sales of computer systems based on its Alpha microprocessors have cooled in recent quarters, Smith said.
"We continue to expect a decline year-on-year with the Alpha business. I think Wall Street is really going to key off Alpha in the future," he said.
On the other hand, sales of workstations and high-end servers may be higher, said Terry Shannon, editor of the newsletter "Shannon Knows DEC."
During the fourth quarter, DEC made headlines with its lawsuit against Intel Corp. DEC alleged that the chipmaker illegally used DEC technology to build the Pentium microprocessor family.
Also during the quarter, a New York broker-dealer held a meeting of institutional shareholders and criticized DEC's lackluster stock price and its marketing and advertising efforts.
Analysts said the lawsuit and the institutional shareholder meeting would have little impact on fourth quarter earnings.

"A customer will just look at a product and decide whether it makes sense for them or not," Stevens said. "The Intel lawsuit -- that's background kind of stuff. It's not something that I would use as part of the decision process."
